source_of_truth: Repo owned capability registry for ERP naming, stock intelligence, and extensibility.

examples: Final roll stock kept for allocate-direct
Ready FG rolls created from stock orders
entries.what_it_means: The system can keep finished rolls in stock and planner can use them directly when the final spec matches.
entries.why: Final-spec matching, stock strategy, route completion, and planner direct-consume flow already exist.
limits: Final spec must match. It is not a substitute for semi-finished reuse.

entries.what_it_means: The system can stop production at a route step and later continue from that stage when the invariant roll properties match.
entries.why: Invariant signature, stop-step compatibility, and continue-from-WIP logic already exist.
limits: Only physically compatible stock can merge into the same reusable pool.

entries.what_it_means: The ERP can classify and report mainstream pouch families while keeping geometry, POD, and material math authoritative.
entries.why: Pouch style taxonomy now sits above the existing geometry and POD model without replacing it.
limits: Classification does not automatically add new physical process behavior.

entries.capability_family: Business-friendly stock naming and variant views
examples: Stock by variant pages in explorer and report pack
entries.what_it_means: Users can see stock by business family first, then variant/size, then exact roll labels.
entries.why: Commercial family taxonomy and shared naming builder now drive explorer, planner labels, PDF, and workbook outputs.
limits: Wrong taxonomy setup will still create bad names. The naming engine cannot fix bad masters automatically.

entries.capability_family: New commercial families and customer-facing naming
entries.what_it_means: You can add new readable business groupings without touching the core math engine.
entries.why: CommercialFamily is a controlled alias layer, not a hardcoded enum.
limits: This changes naming and grouping only, not manufacturing behavior.

entries.what_it_means: You can change how already-supported stock is presented by changing grouping or taxonomy, not physics.
entries.why: Variant-first reporting now sits on top of the physical inventory model.
limits: The same stock cannot be merged if it is not physically interchangeable.

entries.what_it_means: You can add or refine classification and naming for mainstream pouch styles already covered by the current geometry model.
entries.why: Pouch style is now controlled taxonomy rather than free text or hidden logic.
limits: If the style needs a new execution formula or machine behavior, this moves into new-logic territory.

entries.capability_family: New manufacturing process with different execution states
examples: A new converting process with extra approval gates
A machine flow with different input/output object rules
entries.what_it_means: If the factory starts making products through a process the ERP does not model today, code is required.
entries.why: Routing, execution logging, operator actions, and inventory reconciliation depend on physical process rules.
limits: Naming or taxonomy cannot simulate missing process behavior.

entries.capability_family: New reconciliation or physics formula family
examples: Product where weight is not driven by current roll/pouch area logic
Specialty conversion needing different yield math
entries.what_it_means: If the math itself changes, the ERP needs new formulas and tests.
entries.why: Current support is built around flexible film roll/pouch material mass and route-step reconciliation.
limits: Business aliases cannot make unsupported math correct.

examples: Discrete assemblies not covered by roll/bulk/packaging objects
entries.what_it_means: If stock is not a roll, bulk material, packaging stock, or current pouch output, new inventory modeling is required.
entries.why: Planner, warehouse, genealogy, and reports all depend on the object model.
limits: This is a real domain extension, not just a naming change.
